content:
USPS offers lower nonprofit prices for eligible USPS Marketing Mail. If you plan to send church flyers or newsletters, check both your church's authorization and the mailing itself before using those prices.

An IRS exemption does not automatically qualify you for nonprofit postage. USPS makes its own eligibility decision, and nonprofit prices apply only to domestic mail.

---

## Check whether your church qualifies

Religious organizations are an eligible category. USPS includes nonprofit organizations whose primary purpose is conducting religious worship, supporting qualifying religious worship organizations, or teaching a particular religious faith.

Your organizing documents and actual activities must support a qualifying primary purpose. The organization must be nonprofit, and its net income must not benefit a private stockholder or individual. Incidental religious activities alone do not qualify an organization.

You apply using PS Form 3624, Application to Mail at Nonprofit USPS Marketing Mail Prices. Select the category that describes your organization's primary purpose.

---

## Check whether the mailing fits

USPS Marketing Mail is bulk mail. Each mailing must contain at least 200 addressed pieces or 50 pounds of addressed pieces. Individual pieces must weigh less than 16 ounces. There is no single-piece USPS Marketing Mail price.

Flyers, newsletters and bulletins are examples of material sent as USPS Marketing Mail, provided the contents do not require another mail class. Check the complete mailing with your Business Mail Entry Unit, especially if it includes advertising.

<Callout type="important">
These requirements were checked with USPS on October 15, 2026. Before printing or paying postage, confirm current eligibility, preparation rules, prices and fees with USPS. Use its current Notice 123 price list and Business Mail Entry Unit for the mailing you plan to send.
</Callout>

---

## Gather the application documents

Prepare evidence of both your nonprofit status and your qualifying purpose. Publication 417 explains the supporting documents; PS Form 3624 includes the application instructions.

| What USPS needs | What to gather |
|---|---|
| Papers | Your articles of incorporation, constitution or other organizing instrument, including amendments |
| Status | Your IRS exemption letter, or, if unavailable, a complete financial statement from an independent auditor substantiating nonprofit status |
| Work | Bulletins, meeting minutes, brochures or other materials showing your activities, with available financial and budget information |

A statement from a member of your organization is not an acceptable substitute for the independent financial statement. Federal income tax exemption itself is not required to qualify for the postal prices, but you still need the required evidence of eligibility.

Use the organization's complete name consistently on the application and supporting documents. Have a responsible church official sign it. A printer or mailing agent cannot sign for your church.

<Callout type="tip">
Ask your postmaster or Business Mail Entry Unit about documentation questions. A postal specialist may request additional supporting information during review.
</Callout>

---

## Submit and wait for authorization

Submit the completed application and supporting documents to the Post Office where you intend to deposit the mail. Request a date-stamped copy for your records. USPS also describes an online application option through its Business Customer Gateway.

Until USPS authorizes nonprofit prices, pay the applicable regular USPS Marketing Mail postage for a Marketing Mail mailing. If you want to preserve a possible refund while the application is pending, arrange this with the postmaster before mailing. Approval can allow a refund of the eligible difference, subject to USPS rules. First-Class Mail postage is not refundable under this process.

When approved, save the authorization letter. USPS issues a national nonprofit authorization number, which belongs in the appropriate space on each nonprofit mailing's postage statement.

---

## Separate authorization from mailing costs

There is no fee to apply for nonprofit authorization. Mailing permits, annual mailing fees and postage are separate matters.

A mailing permit gives permission to use a particular postage payment method. A permit imprint has an application fee; applying to mail with precanceled stamps or a postage meter has no application fee. Ask USPS which permits and fees apply to your planned payment method and mailing location. USPS describes annual-fee waivers for qualifying full-service automation mailings, so confirm whether a waiver applies.

Your national nonprofit authorization can be used at Post Offices that accept presorted mailings. At a location without PostalOne! access, file PS Form 3623 to confirm authorization before using nonprofit prices there. Ask the receiving office to confirm the arrangements before taking your mail to a new location.

---

## Prepare the mailpiece correctly

Nonprofit mail follows the sorting and preparation rules for regular USPS Marketing Mail. It also needs the proper nonprofit marking, such as NONPROFIT ORG, in the location appropriate to your postage payment method.

Show the authorized organization's name and address on the outside or prominently in the contents. If you include a return address, use the authorized organization's name and complete return address. Ask USPS about a different church name before using it; a doing-business-as name must appear on the authorization.

- [ ] Check the content, piece count and weight against the applicable mailing standards.
- [ ] Confirm the nonprofit marking and organization identification.
- [ ] Prepare the required sorting and postage statement.
- [ ] Enter the national nonprofit authorization number on that statement.

---

## Do not borrow another organization's authorization

Your authorization covers your organization's own mail. It cannot be lent or rented to another organization. A supporting church's authorization does not automatically cover a separate church plant's mail.

Cooperative mailings have their own eligibility rules, including a limited fundraising exception. If another organization shares the mailing's cost, risk or benefit, ask USPS to review the arrangement before claiming nonprofit prices.

<Callout type="warning">
Authorization does not approve every product or advertisement you might include. Have your Business Mail Entry Unit review advertising while you are designing the piece. Check Publication 417 before committing to a print run with promotional inserts.
</Callout>

---

## Keep the authorization and mailing records

Keep your application copy, approval letter and postage statements together. They document the application, authorization and mailings, and postage statements support a refund request when one is available.

USPS revokes nonprofit authorization for nonuse if the authorized organization makes no nonprofit-price mailings during a two-year period. Keep track of your mailing dates, and confirm your authorization before restarting after a long pause.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner."* — 1 Corinthians 14:40 (LSB)
</Callout>

claim_check.notes: Independent Opus review of head 43cbfaf3c3df4647f6bd48c56203496015453075 on 2026-10-15. Re-read all 24 source URLs and matched every factual sentence: eligibility categories and primary-purpose test (Pub 417 2-1, 2-2.1; DMM 703.1), PS Form 3624 title, signer, name and category rules (January 2017 form), documentation (Pub 417 3-1.3, 3-1.4), filing, date-stamped copy and pending-refund rules (Pub 417 3-1.6; DMM 703.1.9), 200 addressed pieces or 50 pounds, under 16 ounces and no single-piece price (Pub 417 4-3.1; Business Mail 101), no application fee, permit and annual-fee rules, national authorization number, PS Form 3623 at non-PostalOne! offices (DMM 703.1.8.1; Pub 417 3-2.2), identification and d.b.a. rules (Pub 417 4-3.2), own-mail and cooperative rules (Pub 417 4-1, 5-1), content restrictions (Pub 417 6-1.2) and two-year nonuse revocation (Pub 417 3-3.1; DMM 703.1.11.4). Notice 123 effective October 04, 2026 confirmed. No dollar rates or fees stated; volatile rules carry the October 15, 2026 as-of callout. 1 Corinthians 14:40 matches lsbible.org word for word. Lint passes with no warnings (1,039 words); desktop and mobile screenshots render all content, the table, checklist and LSB notice. No copied passages beyond form titles and numeric thresholds.

rulings: 2026-10-15 author ruling, resolved: Use current DMM 703.1.8.1 and Publication 417 section 3-2.2 for confirmation at non-PostalOne! locations. Form 3624 January 2017 contains an inconsistent “does participate” sentence; do not repeat it. Publication 417 introductory each-office wording is superseded by its nationwide authorization section and current DMM.

2026-10-15 author ruling, resolved: Omit dollar prices, approval turnaround estimates, delivery timing, EDDM procedures and detailed advertising exceptions. Direct the reader to current USPS guidance; the article is solely A3. No methodology, theology or pastoral-care ruling introduced.
